## Parameter Sensitivity Analysis

<!-- Auto-generated by src/powergrid_benchmark/mintou_planning_sensitivity.py (status: public_simbench_planning_sensitivity_v1). Numbers match evidence/tables/real_sensitivity_sweep.csv. -->

To verify that the comparison in the deterministic vs scenario experiment does not hinge on a fortunate parameter choice, we performed a one-at-a-time parameter sweep around the default configuration. SHIELD-MOEA exposes three influential parameters: the population size $N_p$ (shared by all population-based competitors), the number of worst-case scenarios retained during screening $K$, and the screening period $T_s$ (a re-screen every $T_s$ generations). We swept $N_p \in \{20, 40, 60\}$ (default 40), $K \in \{2, 4, 8\}$ (default 4), and $T_s \in \{3, 5, 10\}$ (default 5). The final evaluation always uses the full disjoint-seed scenario set, so screening parameters can only affect the search, never the scoring.

Each parameter point was re-run with 10 independent seeds under the protocol of the main experiments: identical SimBench-derived problem instance, identical search/evaluation scenario seeds, and the hypervolume of the feasible non-dominated front computed under the same fixed, method-independent normalization bounds, so hypervolumes are directly comparable across parameter points. On the population-size axis the strongest baseline (NSGA-II) was re-run at each matched population size; for the method-specific parameters, which do not affect the baselines, the NSGA-II reference at the default $N_p=40$ is shown. Two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests compare the proposed method against the corresponding NSGA-II reference at every point.

Figure \ref{fig:sensitivity} (panels (a)-(c)) and Table \ref{tab:sensitivity} summarize the sweep.

| Parameter | Value | SHIELD-MOEA HV (mean $\pm$ std) | NSGA-II reference HV | $p$ (MWU) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| population size $N_p$ | 20 | 0.2583 $\pm$ 0.0155 | 0.2360 | 0.0113297 |
| population size $N_p$ | 40 (default) | 0.2674 $\pm$ 0.0108 | 0.2527 | 0.00728456 |
| population size $N_p$ | 60 | 0.2671 $\pm$ 0.0120 | 0.2610 | 0.10411 |
| number of screened worst-case scenarios $K$ | 2 | 0.2715 $\pm$ 0.0062 | 0.2527 | 0.000329839 |
| number of screened worst-case scenarios $K$ | 4 (default) | 0.2658 $\pm$ 0.0108 | 0.2527 | 0.0140193 |
| number of screened worst-case scenarios $K$ | 8 | 0.2701 $\pm$ 0.0079 | 0.2527 | 0.00131494 |
| scenario-screening period $T_s$ | 3 | 0.2688 $\pm$ 0.0074 | 0.2527 | 0.000768539 |
| scenario-screening period $T_s$ | 5 (default) | 0.2687 $\pm$ 0.0085 | 0.2527 | 0.00170625 |
| scenario-screening period $T_s$ | 10 | 0.2671 $\pm$ 0.0121 | 0.2527 | 0.0172575 |

Across the population size $N_p$ axis, the mean hypervolume of SHIELD-MOEA varies between 0.2583 and 0.2674 (a spread of 3.4% of the default-configuration value), with the best mean at population size = 40.

Across the number of screened worst-case scenarios $K$ axis, the mean hypervolume of SHIELD-MOEA varies between 0.2658 and 0.2715 (a spread of 2.1% of the default-configuration value), with the best mean at number of screened worst-case scenarios = 2.

Across the scenario-screening period $T_s$ axis, the mean hypervolume of SHIELD-MOEA varies between 0.2671 and 0.2688 (a spread of 0.6% of the default-configuration value), with the best mean at scenario-screening period = 3.

At every parameter point the mean hypervolume of SHIELD-MOEA remains above the corresponding NSGA-II reference (smallest margin 0.0061 in absolute hypervolume), i.e., no rank reversal occurs anywhere in the swept range. The advantage retains its sign but loses statistical significance at the 0.05 level at population size $N_p$ = 60 ($p$ = 0.10411), which we report for completeness. The total spread of the proposed method's mean hypervolume across all 9 parameter points is 5.0% of the default-configuration value. We conclude that the main comparative result is robust to the tested parameter choices, and that the defaults ($N_p = 40$, $K = 4$, $T_s = 5$) sit in a flat region of the response rather than at a tuned peak.

## Predeclared Formulation Boundary Supplement

Stage `p4_s3_boundary_experiments` adds a separate 1050-run one-at-a-time matrix after equation reconciliation. It varies the budget factor (0.82, 1.00, 1.20), scenario count (8, 16, 32 with $K/|\mathcal S|=1/4$), and the selected-action scale in the survivability equation (0.75, 1.00, 1.25). Five methods receive 30 independent method-specific optimizer seeds per setting. These runs use new disjoint search/evaluation scenario draws and do not replace or pool with the main archive.

Under the primary clipped fixed-bound HV at reference point $1.1^5$, the within-setting SHIELD-minus-NSGA-II+Repair mean gap is positive in all seven settings (0.01013--0.01885; 3.46--7.20%), and every pointwise bootstrap interval lies above zero. The direction is unchanged without clipping and at the predeclared alternative reference point $1.2^5$. Magnitude is not invariant: 441/1050 fronts require low-side clipping, concentrated in the tight-budget and 0.75-survivability-scale settings. The bounds are method-independent but include infeasible singletons, producing a very wide cost range and compressing feasible cost differences.

The mechanism controls remain negative or null evidence. DE-only has a higher mean than the hybrid in all seven settings with every pointwise interval spanning zero; fixed worst-$K$ is unresolved in all seven. Under the tight budget, full-minus-GA-only is -0.00326 with a pointwise interval [-0.00582, -0.00061]. Because these intervals are exploratory and multiplicity-unadjusted, no equivalence or GA-only superiority conclusion is supported. Full values and the immutable manifest are under `evidence/`.
